title: Connector
description: Concrete code implementing one or more capability interfaces. Only the dispatcher instantiates connectors; agents never see them or their secrets.

produces.description: Item kinds (content types) this connector's items carry, versioned (`<kind>/v<N>`, e.g. email/v1). Required for an items.source connector; `bay check` checks it against the `reads:` of every mode whose env binds it (B-6).

entry.description: Python file in the connector folder exposing create(ctx).

login.description: Function in `entry` that `bay auth <connector>` calls (interactive terminal only) with a login context: the connector's declared secrets via the env's provider (secret, store_secret), an Http limited to its declared hosts, open_browser and say.

source.description: Value stamped on every item's `source` by this items.source connector (item ids are <source>:<extId>).

secrets.description: Secret names or globs (X_*). Each must be allowed by the environment.

network.description: Hosts. Each must be in env network.allow.

capabilities.description: Other interfaces this connector calls (bound in the same env).

window.description: How far back the source API can reach (items.source). Older history comes only from the store.

changeFeed.description: items.source: the cursor replays every change since it was taken (new items, label changes, deletions; Gmail history.list), so once a query has a cursor the store always continues from it, sends no deletion checks with it, backfills older items separately with `until` (skipping `storedIds`) until coverage reaches the window start, and re-lists the window when the source answers `cursorExpired`.

exactLabels.description: items.source: every item carries its complete current label set (Gmail labelIds), so the store replaces stored labels instead of adding to them; a removed label then takes the item out of an `in` selector.

costPerPostUsd.description: Price per item this source reads; overrides the mode's costPerPostUsd (e.g. 0 for offline sources). A source with a price above 0 is paid: validate warns about local-only selector fields on it.

selectors.description: items.source: which selector fields (bay/selector.py) this source's native search handles. `native` narrows the fetch, `local` is matched by the store after fetching; a field not listed cannot be expressed (bay check errors). `as` says what a native value means here (e.g. a handle, a List id).

localWith.description: Native fields only: the source matches this field locally when the same selector also sets one of these fields (x-api: `from` together with `in`). Validate warns on a paid source.
